subject: Staging sandbox traffic attribution & credit request
messages:
From: ops@starkapps.com (StarkApps - Platform Ops)
To: ben.carter@redwood.inference
Cc: infra-telemetry@starkapps.com
Date: 2027-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Unexpected charges from staging traffic on Apr 7-10

Hi Ben,

We're seeing a sizable token/usage charge reflected on our April 10 invoice that appears to originate from sandbox/staging hosts. Per our contract and the onboarding notes, staging traffic should be discounted and in some cases flagged as non-chargeable when coming from the VM fleet tagged "staging-*". Can you help us understand why these calls were billed as regular production usage?

Summary:
- Invoice period: Apr 1–10, 2027
- Charge line: "Text generation - tokens" (Apr 7–10 spike)
- Host identifiers in our logs: staging-us-west-2-01..staging-us-west-2-06

I've attached a CSV export from our side with request ids and timestamps. We suspect either the token attribution pipeline attributed requests to the wrong API key or the prefix-caching logic was bypassed during a regional failover.

Can you confirm whether Redwood has a staging entitlement/discount tag applied at the API key or project level? If not, we need a clear path to a retro credit for the affected window.

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Billing & Finance, StarkApps
[attachment: stark_usage_export_apr11.csv (CSV, 1.1MB)]

From: ben.carter@redwood.inference

Hi Emily — thanks for the detailed export. I pulled the initial metering snapshot for your account and forwarded the relevant logs to our infra team. A few quick clarifying Qs so we can triage: 

1) Which API key was used for the staging hosts? (sometimes staging uses project-specific keys that are not tagged)
2) Were any hosts recently migrated between us-west-2 and us-east-1 on Apr 9 (you mention regional failover)?

I'll also ask Lauren from Billing to review the invoice line and determine whether a retroactive credit is appropriate once we confirm attribution. Karthik — looping you in since this affects the renewal conversation next quarter.

I expect we can get a root-cause within 24–48 hrs.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.inference

Cc: ops@starkapps.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference
Date: 2027-04-12T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges from staging traffic on Apr 7-10

Thanks Ben — adding our ledger review notes inline.

Lauren's notes (billing):
- If traffic is confirmed to have been generated by hosts explicitly tagged as staging in the customer's telemetry, we typically apply a pro-rated credit for the disputed window (credit = billed tokens * staging_discount_rate).
- We need the following to approve: 1) evidence of host tags in the customer's telemetry, 2) sample request-ids that match our metering entries, and 3) an explicit list of API keys or service accounts used by staging.

If we get that within 48 hrs we can issue a manual adjustment before the next invoice cycle. If attribution is ambiguous (e.g., same API key used across prod/staging), we will need a compensating reconciliation plan — usually a 30% provisional credit while a longer forensic audit runs.

- Lauren Bishop
Manager, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference

From: infra-telemetry@starkapps.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.inference
Cc: emily.zhao@starkapps.com
Date: 2027-04-12T10:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges from staging traffic on Apr 7-10

Hi Ben / Lauren —

Thanks for the quick reply. We attached the list of request ids and the host tag dump for the Apr 7–10 window. Two notes from our side:

- Staging hosts used the project key proj-stark-staging (we expected Redwood to map this to a staging entitlement).
- On Apr 9 we did a controlled failover to us-east-1 for a subset of staging agents; however DNS TTLs and our orchestration caused some requests to route briefly through us-west-2 gateway instances that are shared with production.

Attached: stark_usage_export_apr11.csv, host_tag_dump_apr09.json, trace_samples.txt

We believe the main issue is API key-level tagging not being mapped in Redwood's attribution layer during cross-region routing. Happy to hop on a call and walk through the trace samples.

— StarkApps Telemetry Team
[attachment: host_tag_dump_apr09.json (JSON, 250KB)]

From: ben.carter@redwood.inference
To: ops@starkapps.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.inference, karthik.iyer@redwood.inference
Date: 2027-04-13T14:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected charges from staging traffic on Apr 7-10

Emily / StarkApps team —

Appreciate the artifacts, they helped us pinpoint the gap. Summary of findings: 

1) Root cause: During the Apr 9 regional failover, certain requests lost the project-level API key header in our edge proxy transiently, which caused attribution to fall back to the gateway's default (production) route. This is a bug in an uncommon code path in our regional gateway handshake.

2) Impact: ~2.8M tokens billed to your account for Apr 9–10 that should have been marked as staging-flagged.

3) Immediate remediation: We patched the gateway to preserve project-key headers across failover and validated with a staged rollout; no further misattribution expected.

4) Compensation: We're issuing a manual credit for the misattributed tokens equal to the billed amount for those tokens (you will see a -$2,120.47 line on the next statement). Per Lauren's note, because your telemetry provided host tags and request-id matches, no provisional reduction is needed.

5) Next steps: I'll create the adjustment ticket and Lauren will post the ledger entry. Karthik, I'll share the incident summary for the renewal pack. Emily — please confirm once you see the credit on your account and reply if you'd like a short post-mortem call this week (15–20 min).

Thanks for the patience — sorry for the disruption.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
